data.name: Bartolomea
data.gender_notes: Bartolomea is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the masculine name Bartholomew, which in Greek means 'son of Tola'. In the Bible, Bartolomew is an apostle who was also known as Nathanael. The name Bartolomea carries the meaning “Daughter of Tola” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Bartolomea usually hope their child will grow to embody daughter of tola and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes devotion and loyalty to one's faith.
data.etymology: Bartolomea belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Daughter of Tola.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bartolomea total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: ברתולומא
in_hebrew.meaning: בַּר תָּלוֹמָא - בן תלמי, פירוש השם הוא בן הארץ
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ברתולומא הוא שילוב של שני מילים בארמית: 'בר' שפירושו בן, ו'תלמי' שפירושו הארץ. השם נגזר מהשם העברי בר תלמי, המוזכר בברית החדשה כחברו של ישוע, בר תלמי, או בשמו המלא, נתנאל בר תלמי. השם משקף את הקשר של הנושא לשמו עם הארץ, ומבטא את המוצא או הקשר שלו לאזור מסוים.

in_greek.name: Βαρτολομαία
in_greek.meaning: Βαρτολομαία - Παράγεται από τον Εβραϊκό όνομα בר תלמי (Bar Talmai), που σημαίνει 'γιος του Talmai'
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βαρτολομαία προέρχεται από το Εβραϊκό όνομα בר תלמי (Bar Talmai), που σημαίνει 'γιος του Talmai'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Βαρθολομαίος (Βαρθolomeαῖος) αναφέρεται ως ένας από τους δώδεκα αποστόλους του Ιησού. Το όνομα συνδέεται με την παράδοση της Εκκλησίας και αντανακλά την πνευματική κληρονομιά των πρώτων Χριστιανών.

in_latin.name: Bartolomea
in_latin.meaning: Bartolomea - Filia Bartholomaei, interpretatur Terrae filia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Bartolomea derivatur a nomine Hebraeo בר תלמי (Bar Talmai), quod significat 'filius Talmai' vel 'terrae filius'. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc associatur cum Bartholomaeo, uno ex duodecim apostolis Iesu Christi. Nomen reflectit traditionem ecclesiasticam et hereditatem spiritualem primorum Christianorum.

in_english.name: Bartolomea
in_english.meaning: Daughter of Bartholomew, meaning 'son of the earth' or 'of the land'
in_english.long_meaning: The name Bartolomea originates from the Hebrew name בר תלמי (Bar Talmai), meaning 'son of Talmai' or 'of the earth'. It is associated with Bartholomew, one of Jesus' twelve apostles, mentioned in the New Testament. The name signifies a connection to the land or earth, reflecting a spiritual grounding. Historically, the name has been used in Christian tradition to denote a follower or descendant of Bartholomew, embodying qualities of earthly devotion and spiritual richness.

data.cultural_impact: Bartolomea was often used as a feminine form of Bartholomew in Spain and Italy during the Middle Ages. It is an uncommon name nowadays, but it holds a rich cultural history. In some regions, Saint Bartholomew is the patron saint of butchers, leatherworkers, farmers, and travelers. Thus, the name Bartolomea may be associated with these professions or industries.
data.spiritual_significance: Nathanael, one of the twelve apostles, was known for his quick faith. When he heard that Jesus was the King of Israel, Nathanael exclaimed, "Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the King of Israel" (John 1:49). The name Bartolomea is a reminder of the power of faith and the importance of recognizing and declaring Jesus as the Son of God and the King of our lives. It is a name that inspires us to be quick to believe and to profess our faith in the Lord.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bartolomea, derived from St. Bartholomew, symbolizes endurance and devotion. As a disciple who was reportedly flayed alive for his faith, she embodies the strength to bear suffering and remain steadfast in spiritual commitment.

historical_references.reference: Bartolomea of the Martyrs, who is also known as St. Bartholomew, was a disciple of Jesus Christ. He is believed to have preached in India, Armenia, and Greece. Later, he was martyred in Albanopolis, Armenia, during the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius (138-161 AD).

St. Bartholomew the Apostle is also identified as Nathanael, one of the twelve apostles. He is believed to have been present at the multiplication of the loaves and fishes and the preaching of the Sermon on the Mount. Later, he was martyred in Armenia during the reign of Emperor Leo I (457-474 AD).

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Bartolomea, a feminine variation of Bartolomeo, has seen a modern resurgence in various contexts, particularly within the Latinx community and feminist circles. On social media platforms like Instagram and Twitter, many individuals with the name Bartolomea share their experiences and stories, promoting diversity and inclusivity. Meanwhile, on YouTube, there are educational channels dedicated to the history and significance of Hispanic names, including Bartolomea. These trends reflect a growing appreciation for Latinx heritage and a push towards gender equality and representation.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Mary Bartolomea in London, United Kingdom credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Bartolomea, which means "Daughter of Tola". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
